We need to detect whether the argument was a branch or not, and then immediately throw an error, if it was a branch and a pr was not found.  
`PullRequestForBranch` also returned a `NotFoundError`, and it had to be distinguished form the `NotFoundError` returned form `PullRequestByNumber`

---

```

```

```

```

issue_context.title: Allow users to view an issue or PR even the object provided is incorrect
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

Issues and PRs have unique numbers across them, and therefore GitHub.com redirects you to the right place even if you put `/issue` in the url when you mean `/pull`

### Proposed solution

For viewing issues or PRs, if you use `gh issue view [number]` with a PR number or `gh pr view [number]` with an issue number, it still allows you to view the issue or PR with that number, even if the object is incorrect. This should also work with `--web`.

### Additional context

For an example of this on GitHub.com, this URL redirects to the PR, even though issues is in the URL: https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/1114
comments: I would like to take this up

I feel we should also show a warning to the users, saying that its a pr, not an issue, or vice versa.
Something like: `warning: #1114 is a pull request, not an issue`

Or, we could simply say: `#1114 is a pull request, not an issue`, and prompt: `Continue? (y/n)`
If the user says yes, we can internally call the pr command.
@AliabbasMerchant Thanks! 🤔 I'd be fine with a warning and and being able to continue, though I'm not certain it's completely necessary.

I would just say that we should display the information based on the number regardless of the type. I think warnings and errors should be employed when they bring value to a user, but in this case I don't see how a person gets value from being informed that `#1114` is not an issue but a PR. Maybe `gh pr view 1114` should display a warning when passed in an issue, but `gh issue view ...` should never warn since PRs are basically Issues (i.e. they have the same fields and can do everything that issues can).

With upcoming aliases work, I would personally be interested in creating an alias for `issue view --web` called `open` that I could simply pass in a number of any issue or PR to. Right now that's not possible due to preconditions.

review_comments:
Right now, I'm not a fan of the approach where after an API error we fall back to looking up the object of a different type. Ideally, we would always run a single API request with an issue number as input and return either an issue or a PR object. I realize that this would complicate both our current query logic and return types from functions, but we could potentially do some type-switching on the return types.

@AliabbasMerchant Do you think there would be merit to this approach?

I think that if the API provides an in-built method to handle both of them in a single call/method, it could make sense to do so, But still, printing them would definitely require separate logic for both, which could become quite cumbersome.  
And I agree with you, it could complicate our current query logic if we try to combine them.  
I tried some kind of type-switching/unifying on the return types [here](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/1153#issuecomment-642862574), but personally I was not satisfied with the result.
I had kept the print function calls separate, as they represent 2 completely different paths to take
